sources.title: A Faster Approximation Algorithm for the Steiner Problem in Graphs
A Fast Algorithm for Steiner Trees

workspace.meaning: Bounded storage for at most eight vertices, fourteen original edges, twenty-eight terminal pairs, multi-source distances/owners/predecessors, crossing-edge witnesses, DSU state, expanded-edge flags, final tree degrees/queue, and staged output.

primary_steps: Multi-source Dijkstra from all terminals computes each vertex's nearest-terminal region; equal distances choose lower terminal ID, and equal same-owner predecessor choices choose lower (predecessor vertex, edge ID).

Scan each original edge crossing two regions and create the candidate terminal edge of length dist(u)+weight(u,v)+dist(v); retain the minimum candidate per unordered terminal pair, breaking ties by oriented endpoints and edge ID.
Run Kruskal on the sparse terminal graph, with ties by candidate weight, terminal IDs, endpoints, and original edge ID.

Expand each selected candidate through its two predecessor paths and crossing edge; compute a minimum spanning tree of the union with ties by (original edge weight, edge ID), then iteratively delete nonterminal leaves.
profile.complexity: O(n^2 + m log m) on this bounded profile; array-scan Dijkstra is O(n^2+m), bounded edge sorting is O(m log m), path expansion is O(n^2), and final tree pruning is O(n+m). The paper's asymptotic implementation bound is not claimed.
profile.independent_reference: Per-terminal Bellman-Ford relaxation and predecessor reconstruction, followed by exhaustive enumeration of candidate-graph spanning trees and exhaustive enumeration of the expanded-union spanning tree; this avoids the primary's multi-source Dijkstra and Kruskal transition structure.
profile.duplicate_rationale: Distinct from steiner_tree_subset_dp, which optimizes exactly by terminal-subset dynamic programming, and steiner_tree_gain_greedy, which chooses among a supplied family of full components by gain. This profile uses Voronoi partitioning and crossing-edge sparsification to obtain a terminal MST witness. It is a bounded deterministic implementation of Mehlhorn's construction and makes no approximation-ratio claim beyond the source theorem.
